summary.text: Kristen McDonald Rivet is the Democratic incumbent, seeking a second term. Before Congress she worked in education and early-childhood policy, served on the Bay City Commission and represented the 35th District in the Michigan Senate. According to her official biography, her priorities include cutting taxes for working and middle-class families and lowering costs for groceries, housing, prescription drugs and child care.

paragraphs.text: Kristen McDonald Rivet was born in 1970 in Portland, Michigan, per Wikipedia. According to her official biography, she was raised in a small farm town, where her father worked in construction and her mother stayed home, and she and her sisters were the first generation in the family to attend college.
She earned a bachelor's degree in history from Michigan State University in 1992 and a master's degree in education and public administration from the University of Michigan-Flint.

McDonald Rivet began her career in early-childhood and education policy, including as executive director of Michigan Head Start, chief of staff of the Michigan Department of Education and vice president of The Skillman Foundation, according to her official biography.
She later worked as vice president of Michigan Future, Inc., president and CEO of Greater Midland, Inc., and chief strategy officer of the Michigan Health Improvement Alliance.
In Bay City she held local office, first on the city's Charter Commission and then on the Bay City Commission.

Voters elected her to the Michigan Senate (District 35) in November 2022, defeating Annette Glenn (R). She served from 2023 to 2025 as assistant majority floor leader and sat on committees including Appropriations and Education and Career Readiness.
McDonald Rivet won Michigan's 8th District in 2024 after the retirement of Rep. Dan Kildee, defeating Paul Junge (R), and took office in January 2025.
In the U.S. House she serves on the Agriculture Committee and the Transportation and Infrastructure Committee, and she was elected Freshman Leadership Representative to the New Democratic Coalition.
She advanced unopposed from the August 4, 2026 Democratic primary. According to her official biography, she lives in Bay City with her husband, Joseph, and has six children.
